method: Storms: consecutive GHCN-Daily snowfall days at the nearest reporting station(s) summed; total >= 10 cm. Scenes: Sentinel-2 L2A passes 1-10 days after the storm's last snow day, with no new snowfall > 0.5 cm in between, block >= 90% clear by SCL, and block median snow fraction >= 0.25. Only the block bbox (+40 m) is window-read. NDSI = (B03 - B11)/(B03 + B11) on the 20 m B11 grid (B03 averaged 2x2); snow fraction = clip(0.06 + 1.21*NDSI, 0, 1) (Salomonson & Appel linear form), forced to 0 where SCL is water. Each roof ring is intersected exactly with the 20 m pixels (area-weighted mean). Anomaly = roof snow fraction minus the median of the other roofs in the block on the same scene (needs >= 2 other roofs). early_melt_share = share of observations with anomaly < -0.10; sign_p = one-sided sign test of anomaly < 0. Flag 'faster-melting roof (possible heat loss)' needs >= 4 observations, early_melt_share >= 0.6, median anomaly <= -0.10 and sign_p <= 0.1 (ties within 0.005 excluded). Apron = mapped driveway lines (only where block files hold them) buffered 1.5 m, compared with the median of open ground pixels (no roof).
limits: A 20 m pixel is 400 m2; a typical house roof (100-250 m2) fills a quarter to a half of one pixel, so every roof value is mixed with yard, street, trees and neighbouring roofs ('mixed': true).
Neighbouring houses often share the same pixels, which pulls their values together and hides real differences.
Faster snow loss also comes from steep or south-facing pitches sliding/sun-melting, dark roofing, roof wind scour, shovelling, or trees/shadows in the pixel; heat loss is only one possible reason.
Driveways mapped as lines are ~3 m wide: far below one pixel. A clear driveway is most often shovelled or ploughed, not heated.
Snowfall is a station measurement up to tens of km away; local totals differ.
Few qualifying scenes per winter (clouds follow storms), so observation counts are small.
